overview: This file documents the commercial plans of Wilma Maybelle Hosken, head of the Hosken Trading Company, and the U.S. State Department’s response to her request for assistance obtaining bank credit. Two closely related memoranda record her proposed cooperation with Tokyo’s Hoshi Pharmaceutical Company to establish a cinchona plantation in colonial Taiwan, market quinine outside Japan, purchase menthol and pyrethrum, and export railway materials to Manchuria; the Department declined to endorse these private ventures but arranged a meeting with a First Import-Export Bank official. An accompanying newspaper clipping profiles Hosken as a widowed American exporter who divided her time between New York and Shanghai and sold locomotives, rails, aircraft, cameras, and other modern equipment in China.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Hosken’s pharmaceutical and railway ventures
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs (initialed “H. DLY”)
subfiles.about: Records Wilma Hosken’s request for Department of State support in securing bank credit for pharmaceutical purchases and railway exports connected with Japan, Taiwan, and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Hosken described a proposed partnership with the Hoshi Pharmaceutical Company to establish a cinchona plantation in Formosa, deposit money with the Bank of Taiwan, and receive exclusive rights to sell Hoshi quinine outside Japan. She also wanted to purchase menthol and pyrethrum and export railway materials to Manchuria, but said the quinine investment would leave her unable to finance the other ventures. The Department’s representative characterized the projects as purely commercial, declined to recommend them to the First Import-Export Bank, and arranged a meeting with Major Hall without offering an endorsement.

subfiles.title: Duplicate draft of memorandum on Hosken’s commercial proposals
subfiles.about: Provides a second, slightly variant version of the memorandum concerning Hosken’s proposed quinine, menthol, pyrethrum, and railway-material transactions.
subfiles.summary: This version repeats Hosken’s plan for a cinchona plantation in Formosa and an exclusive foreign-sales agency for quinine produced by Hoshi, whose name is once misread in the OCR as “Yoshi.” It also records her contemplated purchases of menthol and pyrethrum and proposed railway-material exports to Manchuria. As in the first memorandum, the Department refused to judge or endorse the commercial merits of the projects but arranged for Major Hall to receive Hosken.

subfiles.title: Newspaper profile of exporter W. M. Hosken
subfiles.about: Profiles Wilma Hosken as a New York–Shanghai businesswoman selling American industrial and aviation equipment in China.
subfiles.summary: Engle portrays Hosken as the widowed head of the Hosken Trading Company and an experienced transpacific exporter who represented American manufacturers in China. Her reported sales included locomotives, steel rails, Fairchild aerial cameras, airplanes, parachutes, and Lockheed Electra aircraft, with Chao Fong Li cited as a Shanghai consignee. The article presents her work as part of China’s modernization, contrasts New York and Shanghai, and invokes Li Po and the early Wusong–Shanghai railway; the final portion is substantially garbled in the OCR.

interest: The file joins an internal diplomatic record to a popular-press portrait of the same businesswoman, making it possible to compare official caution with public celebration of American commercial expansion in East Asia. It is particularly useful for studying women in interwar international trade, proposed pharmaceutical development in Japanese-ruled Taiwan, and the commercial networks connecting the United States, Japan, China, and Manchuria. The two versions of the State Department memorandum also preserve small drafting and copying differences that may help reconstruct departmental procedure and evaluate OCR reliability.
